resources.string: Flick your toy players and score before the clock runs out.
Race to the goals, or play against the clock. A tie goes to sudden death.
Teams take turns to flick one figure, and the table settles before the next turn. No clock, for players who can\'t play at speed.
Flick it out with a computer opponent.
You and a computer team mate against two computers.
Two players share this device, one at each end of the pitch.
Up to four players share this device. Computers fill empty places.
Swipe to serve and rally, and win the point.
A short race to points, or real games and sets.
The ball waits for your swing and your player is always in place, so only direction and power matter. For players who can\'t play in real time.
Two players share this device, one at each end of the court.
Pull back from one of your figures and let go to flick it at the ball. A longer pull is a harder kick.
A figure can be flicked again once it stops. Keep your keeper near the goal.
Too fast? Turn on Turn-based assist in the setup to take turns without a clock.
Your player runs to the ball by itself. Swipe toward the net just as the ring closes.
Swipe left or right of straight for the angle, and faster for a harder, deeper shot.
Too fast? Turn on Relaxed timing in the setup and the ball waits for your swing.

Score more goals than the other team.

Pull back from one of your figures, like a slingshot, and let go: it shoots the way you pulled, harder the longer the pull. Knock the ball into the goal at the far end. A figure can be flicked again once it has stopped, and the keeper springs back to the goal by itself.

Everyone flicks at the same time, so be quick. The first team to the goal target wins, or the team with most goals when the clock runs out. A tie goes to sudden death.

Turn-based assist, in the game setup, removes the clock: the teams take turns, one flick each, and the table settles in between. With a screen reader on, a panel of buttons replaces the drag: choose a figure, an aim and a power, then press Flick.
Time is up and it is level. Sudden death: the next goal wins.
Pull back from a figure and let go to flick it.
A player has left the match.
That figure belongs to another player.
It is not your team\'s turn.
That figure is still moving. Wait for it to stop.
A player has left, so the match cannot go on.

Win the point, the game and the match.

Your player runs to the ball by itself. You choose the shot and its moment with one swipe: swipe toward the net, to the left or right of straight for the angle, and faster for a harder, deeper shot. A ring closes around the spot where the ball will be hit; let go just as it closes. A swipe that is early or late lands long, short or wide, and a very early or late one misses.

To serve, the ball is tossed for you: swipe as it reaches the top and land it in the opposite service box. Two faults lose the point. In a rally the ball may bounce once on your side before you hit it.

Scoring is real tennis (0, 15, 30, 40, advantage, games and sets) or a short race to a number of points.

Relaxed timing, in the game setup, makes the ball wait for your swing and keeps your player in place, so only direction and power matter. With a screen reader on, a panel of buttons replaces the swipe.
